Sounds like you never tried Linux and are some M$ fanboy who discredits something he doesn't know.

Drivers

The drivers for your hardware are in the kernel. Distros don't really do shit for drivers. There are some third-party drivers (nvidia, broadcom bleeding-edge network drivers), but 99.9999% of what you need is in the kernel.

As far as which distro to use:

You're probably gonna want to use Fedora. RedHat is driving the Linux ecosystem, (SystemD, GNOME, Wayland, etc.), and they're pretty current with software and kernel updates (which takes care of the majority of your driver problems).

I recommend Fedora over RedHat because it's bascially the same thing, only you're not paying for a support contract. You'll get the GNOME desktop by default (pointy-clicky, terminal blegh), modern display support with Wayland. You don't have any legacy habits built up, so SystemD won't make you want to vomit in your shorts. Built in Docker support coughMobycough.

Caveats

If you haven't installed linux in a while, I think you're going to be pleasantly surprised. There are a few edge cases that pride themselves on being difficult to install (arch, gentoo, etc. -- and they're not really that hard) but, for the most part, it's a fairly straightforward process.

Generally, I can have a linux install up and running in significantly less time than Windows. That's not some neck-beard bragging bullshit either, it's really a lot easier. Pick your timezone, set a user/password and that's pretty much it. The partitioning is guided, the recommended software install default is safe, it installs and reboots into your new system. You log in and get to work.

Software upgrades through the 'Software Center' are point and click. No OS registration or telemetry sent back to the home office. Pretty much everything works out of the box.

If you have an Nvidia video card, you're probably going to have some problems. If you want to play games, it's gotten a lot better, but you're probably going to have some problems. If you have to run specific Windows software, Wine has gotten significantly better but, you're going to have some problems.

All that being said, it's not fucking windows. If you go in with the mindset of, "This isn't like Windows, it's fucking stupid" you're going to have a bad time. Shit is going to be a little bit different. This probably doesn't apply to you, since you have a background with UNIX, but it might help the next asshole who reads this comment.

So go give Fedora a try and come back and let us know how it went.
